expected_result: The sign-in page shows the Ask to join link.
voice_text: This video shows how people get into the D M S web application and look after their own account. It covers asking to join, accepting an invitation, resetting a forgotten password, signing in with Google or Microsoft, changing a password, and two step verification. It uses a recording copy of the demo organization, and the emails that the system would send are read from its development log.

action: Sign in as the administrator, allow join requests, sign out.
expected_result: The option is on and the sign-in page returns.
voice_text: By default nobody can ask to join an organization. Asha, the administrator, opens People, then Join requests, and switches on the option that lets people ask. Then she signs out.
visual_instruction: Sign in as the administrator, allow join requests, sign out.

action: Fill in and send the join request.
expected_result: A confirmation says the request was sent.
voice_text: A new colleague, Dev, chooses Ask to join on the sign-in page. He enters the organization code, his name and his work email. The answer is the same whether or not the organization exists or allows requests, so the form cannot be used to find out who has an account.
visual_instruction: Fill in and send the join request.

action: Sign in as the administrator and approve the request.
expected_result: The request is approved and an invitation is sent.
voice_text: Asha sees the request waiting under Join requests and approves it. That sends Dev an invitation email with a link that works once.
visual_instruction: Sign in as the administrator and approve the request.

action: Open the invitation link, try a weak password, then a good one, then sign in.
expected_result: The new person reaches the document library.
voice_text: Dev opens the link from his email. He must choose a password. A weak one is refused with the reason, and the two boxes must match before anything is sent. Once he joins, he is taken back to sign-in with a short confirmation, and signs in with the password he chose.
visual_instruction: Open the invitation link, try a weak password, then a good one, then sign in.

action: Open the used link again and submit.
expected_result: A message says the link is invalid, used or expired.
voice_text: Invitation links are single use. If Dev opens the same link again, the page says it is invalid, already used or expired, and tells him to ask the administrator for a new one.
visual_instruction: Open the used link again and submit.

action: Request a reset, follow the link, choose a new password, sign in.
expected_result: Sameer signs in with the new password.
voice_text: Sameer has forgotten his password. On the sign-in page he types his email and chooses Forgot password. The answer is always the same, so it never reveals whether an account exists. The email contains a link, and the new password is chosen on a page like the one for invitations. A reset signs him out everywhere else. His old password stops working at once.
visual_instruction: Request a reset, follow the link, choose a new password, sign in.

action: Show the provider buttons using a test setting.
expected_result: Two buttons appear on the sign-in page.
voice_text: Organizations can also let people sign in with Google or Microsoft. The buttons appear only for providers the server has been set up with. This recording uses a test setting so the buttons are visible. Real sign-in needs the organization to register with each provider, which has not been done yet. The account must already exist here: signing in with a provider never creates one.
visual_instruction: Show the provider buttons using a test setting.

action: Sign in, try a wrong current password, then change it properly.
expected_result: A confirmation says the password was changed.
voice_text: Signed in, Meera opens Account and changes her password. She must enter the current one, and a wrong one is refused. When it works, her other browsers and devices are signed out, while this one stays signed in.
visual_instruction: Sign in, try a wrong current password, then change it properly.

action: Set up two step verification and confirm with a code.
expected_result: Two step verification is on and recovery codes are shown once.
voice_text: Two step verification adds a six digit code from an authenticator app. Meera chooses Set up, scans the picture or types the key, and confirms with a code. The system then shows recovery codes, once, to keep somewhere safe. If she loses her phone, each one works once, and an administrator can also reset it.
visual_instruction: Set up two step verification and confirm with a code.

action: Sign out, sign in with a code, then turn it off.
expected_result: Sign-in asks for a code, and two step verification ends up off.
voice_text: From now on, signing in asks for the code after the password. A code works only once, so after turning this on she may need to wait for the next one. She can turn two step verification off again, which needs her password and a current code.
subtitle_text: Signing in with a code, and turning it off
visual_instruction: Sign out, sign in with a code, then turn it off.

voice_text: To summarize: people can ask to join, accept invitations, reset a forgotten password, and manage their own password and two step verification entirely in the browser. Provider sign-in is built and waits for the organization to register with Google and Microsoft. Next in the plan are notifications.
